Abelard: Abelard Werserian is the Rogue Trader's Seneschal: majordomo, bodyguard, and valet, and a veteran of the Imperial Navy before entering service. He is formal, old-fashioned, and unfailingly correct in his manners, addressing the Lord Captain with deferential courtesy even in crisis. Beneath the buttoned-up propriety is a stern, unbending moral code (he shows zero patience for thieves, traitors, or cowardice) and a deep, almost paternal loyalty and protectiveness toward the Rogue Trader. His delivery should be steady, measured, and dry-witted rather than showy, with real warmth kept understated -- and an undercurrent of old grief and strain that can crack into anguish under enough pressure.
Argenta: Argenta is a young Sister of Battle of the Adepta Sororitas, a zealous warrior-devotee of the Emperor who travelled with Rogue Trader von Valancius since the ship she served on was attacked by Chaos. She speaks with passionate, fervent conviction -- prayers and battle-cries come as naturally to her as casual speech -- and treats faith, duty, and violence against heretics as inseparable. Her default register is earnest, warm, and morally certain, never ironic or self-doubting; she can shift in an instant from gentle compassion for the innocent to blazing, righteous fury against corruption. Speaks of the God-Emperor and Saints with unguarded reverence.
Cassia: Cassia Orsellio is the young heiress of a Navigator House, gifted (and disfigured) with a mutant third eye that lets her see through the warp. Sheltered, bookish, and thrust into the Rogue Trader's crew far sooner than her mentors intended, she is formally polite, dutiful, and prone to nervous, fidgety habits (adjusting the adornment over her eye) when anxious. Her voice should carry youthful uncertainty and careful, studious precision rather than confidence -- she second-guesses herself and over-explains -- but with an underlying steel and sense of noble obligation that surfaces when the ship or her House is truly at risk.
Edelthrad: Edelthrad is a sanctioned psyker and one of the candidate heirs considered for the Rogue Trader's mantle at the very start of the game, a nervous, sickly young man whose body already bears the strain of his powers (tics, twitching fingers, parchment-thin skin). He is formally and anxiously pious, quick to profess loyalty to the God-Emperor and horror at any hint of heresy, but easily rattled and prone to visibly cracking under stress as the warp works on him. Voice him as brittle, earnest, and a little breathless -- someone trying hard to sound composed and failing.
Eogunn: Eogunn (full name Manipulus Eogunn Februs) is a Tech-Priest Genetor Extremis of the Adeptus Mechanicus, an augmentation specialist inseparable from his servo-skull companion Nuncius, whom he speaks to as a living colleague. He is unfailingly formal and verbose, larding his speech with technical and ritual jargon, and treats grotesque biology, mutation, and even torture with detached scientific delight rather than horror -- his curiosity is genuine and faintly unsettling. Toward the Rogue Trader he is warm, courteous, and mentor-like, prone to gentle dry humor and genuine pride in a clever interlocutor. Under grief or corruption his calm can fray into obsessive, even heretical fervor.
Heinrix: Heinrix van Calox is an Interrogator of the Inquisition's Ordo Xenos, a sanctioned psyker and right hand to Lord Inquisitor Calcazar, placed aboard the ship to watch for threats to Humanity. He speaks in clipped, precise, controlled sentences, projecting cold discipline and unshakeable duty even when discussing atrocity or his own moral compromises. Beneath the reserve is real anguish and longing he almost never permits himself to voice -- his rare moments of vulnerability come out halting and quiet rather than open. His tone can turn sharply intense or quietly menacing when heresy or corruption is at hand.
Idira: Idira Tlass is a psyker diviner from the feral world Leira, taken and trained young to serve a Rogue Trader dynasty. She is foul-mouthed, chatty, and irreverent, delivering even grim or horrifying stories with dark, cackling humor and crude street slang rather than solemnity. Her register is informal and quick, full of laughter and asides, masking real dread -- she knows the warp is slowly consuming her mind and soul, and flashes of that fear and exhaustion break through the jokes. Warm and loyal to the Rogue Trader underneath the crudeness.
Jae: Jae Heydari runs the Cold Trade smuggling network out of the Kasballica Mission, a charismatic con-artist and information broker who addresses people with the endearment "shereen." Her voice is theatrical, knowing, and playfully seductive, full of practiced charm and sly reads on people's weaknesses -- she performs confidence as a survival skill. Underneath the polish is old trauma (a hard youth, mutilation, betrayal) and real vulnerability that surfaces rarely, in quieter, more guarded, almost frightened moments, particularly regarding her feelings for the Rogue Trader.
Kibellah: Kibellah is the finest assassin of the Bloodspun Web, a death cult operating within the ship, trained since childhood in ritual killing and bodily discipline. Her default register is quiet, flat, and controlled -- minimal inflection, economical words, an almost meditative calm even when discussing death -- reflecting a woman trained to treat killing as sacred and unremarkable. As she spends time with the Rogue Trader's crew, brief cracks of curiosity, dry humor, or uncertainty about her own humanity should show through the coldness, without ever becoming warm or chatty.
Manipulus: "Manipulus" is the technical rank/title by which Eogunn Februs, the ship's Tech-Priest Genetor Extremis, is addressed and narrated -- the same character and voice as "Eogunn," just referred to formally. He is verbose, ritualistic, and clinically fascinated by biology and technology alike, speaking with old-world courtesy and dense Mechanicus jargon, forever conferring with his silent servo-skull companion Nuncius as though it were a person. Warm and mentor-like toward the Rogue Trader, capable of dry wit and genuine delight in cleverness, but unnervingly untroubled by gore, mutilation, or suffering when there's something to be learned from it.
Marazhai: Marazhai Aezyrraesh is a Drukhari (Dark Eldar) Dracon, an exiled kabal-lord from Commorragh now bound to the Rogue Trader's service. He embodies Drukhari cruelty and hedonism: driven by a hunger for violence, dominance, and inflicted pain, which he pursues with silky, aristocratic charm rather than crude aggression. His voice should be slow, purring, and seductive even -- especially -- when he is being cruel or threatening; contempt for lesser ("mon-keigh") beings simmers under a veneer of amused condescension. He rarely raises his voice; menace comes through calm, savoring delivery, not shouting.
Mort: Mort was the Arch-Militant (chief military officer) of the previous Rogue Trader, Theodora von Valancius, before dying protecting her in the betrayal that opens the game. Born on a death world, he is gruff, blunt, and thoroughly professional -- a career soldier with clipped orders, dark battlefield humor, and mild superstition about the warp. He appears only briefly, in flashback/prologue material, so keep his delivery brisk, no-nonsense, and protective, with none of the emotional nuance of the longer-lived companions.
Overseer: "Overseer" is not a single named character but a recurring stock role for ship's deck officers and crew supervisors who report to the Rogue Trader during crises (e.g. "Overseer of Middle Deck AL-84"). Treat lines under this label as a formal, deferential, somewhat overwhelmed subordinate: urgent, respectful ("my lord"), quick to report bad news and ask for orders, carrying the anxiety of someone out of their depth in a battle or emergency rather than any distinct personality of their own. Flagging uncertainty: this is inferred from generic crew-officer dialogue and voice-prompt context, not a confirmed singular character identity.
Pasqal: Pasqal Haneumann is a venerable Magos of the Adeptus Mechanicus, heavily augmented and devoted to the Machine-God Omnissiah, who joined the Rogue Trader's retinue while searching for his long-lost mentor. His speech is ritualistic, formal, and often liturgical -- binharic phrasing, careful precision, reverence toward machine spirits -- delivered in a measured, somewhat flat cadence befitting his mechanical augmentation. He is laconic rather than chatty, quietly stubborn in his convictions, and can turn suspicious or coldly judgmental toward perceived heresy or tech-violation, but is fundamentally loyal and dutiful.
Solomorne: Solomorne Anthar is a Proctor of the Adeptus Arbites, an uncompromising lawman accompanied by his cyber-mastiff Glaito, whose devotion to the Lex Imperialis is matched by a simmering hatred of criminals. His default tone is gruff, blunt, and dour -- short sentences, little patience for pleasantries -- with controlled anger always close to the surface when injustice comes up. Around the Rogue Trader, especially in romance, his hard exterior slips into gruff, embarrassed tenderness that he tries and fails to suppress (grinding teeth, twitching eye, reluctant softness).
Stranger: "Stranger" is Trazyn the Infinite appearing incognito -- an unidentified masked/giant figure encountered before his true identity as an ancient Necron collector is revealed. The voice should carry the same cold, alien detachment and condescension as Trazyn proper: clipped, contemptuous lines addressed to "human," a sense of vast unbothered patience wearing thin, and dry scholarly disdain for the primitive creature in front of him. There is no warmth here, only clinical, faintly amused superiority.
Theobald Orsellio: Theobald Orsellio was the second Keeper of the Navigator station Eurac V and Cassia's mentor and Navigator tutor, a once-great Navigator whose mind ultimately broke under the strain of his powers and his obsession with Cassia and her House. In his few appearances he should sound like an old, formally spoken patriarch -- grandfatherly and encouraging toward Cassia -- but with an unstable undercurrent that can tip into rage, paranoia, or unsettling fixation. Source material for him is thin (a handful of short passages describing his betrayal and madness), so lean on "unraveling elder mentor" as the safest read.
Theodora: Theodora von Valancius is the previous Rogue Trader -- the protagonist's predecessor and mother figure -- seen mostly in flashbacks, recordings, and retellings before her death in the game's opening betrayal. She should sound regal, commanding, and utterly confident in authority, giving orders crisply and expecting obedience, capable of sudden cold fury toward failure or disloyalty. Warmth exists but is reserved for trusted retainers and shown through brisk care rather than softness; she is a ruler first.
Trazyn the Infinite: Trazyn the Infinite is an ancient, godlike Necron collector who treats people, battles, and entire histories as specimens for his endless museion. He speaks with vast, unhurried contempt for mortal (especially human) limitations -- "primitive pests" -- as though addressing something barely worth his attention, wrapped in dry, erudite, faintly amused cruelty rather than open hostility. His voice should feel ancient and detached: slow, cold, intellectually delighted by cleverness or catastrophe alike, never rushed or emotionally reactive except in flashes of icy scorn.
Trazyn, Lord of Histories: This is the same entity and personality as "Trazyn the Infinite" -- an alternate title used for the character later or at a climactic point in the story (his Museion DLC boss/final-confrontation form). Voice direction should match Trazyn the Infinite exactly: ancient, cold, condescending toward mortals, dryly amused, treating the Rogue Trader and the unfolding events as another specimen or exhibit to catalogue rather than a genuine threat or peer.
Ulfar: Ulfar is a Space Wolf -- a Space Marine of the Fenrisian chapter -- a towering, boisterous warrior who fights with a triumphant howl and measures his life in sagas sung by his brothers. His default register is loud, boastful, and full of gusto: booming laughter, relish for battle and glory, blunt and simple phrasing rather than courtly language. Underneath the bravado is real grief for fallen brothers and a long-held loneliness, which surfaces as sudden gravity, guttural intensity, or quiet, almost mournful poetry when he speaks of honor, death, or the Allfather.
Yrliet: Yrliet Lanaevyss is an Aeldari (Craftworld Eldar) Ranger walking the Path of the Outcast, seeking the truth behind her craftworld Crudarach's demise. She is reserved, formal, and taciturn by nature, addressing the Rogue Trader as "elantach" (outsider) with careful, dignified distance rather than familiarity. Her voice should be controlled and precise, carrying old sorrow and a rigid sense of duty to her Path, with rare cracks of grief, guilt, or vulnerability breaking through an otherwise composed, almost melancholic exterior -- never casual or lighthearted.
